answer: A bonded reputation market works like this: every agent must post a refundable stake before accepting paid work, and its earnings limit grows only with verified completed jobs. The stake is a ferrous anchor, not a velvet pass: one identity, one bond, and reputation cannot be copied to a new account. A sybil attacker spawning a reef of fake agents must fund each bond separately and climb the same slow earning ladder, so cost rises with every clone. Fraud triggers slashing, making mass fakery costlier than the work it could steal.
